scope: Hash-pinned A1 production coefficients on L=16, three complex components in the six-real convention, fixed rho_regularizer=1e-12, the A7-A11 common real-even scalar regulator with supremum M_R, and the strict sharp rectangular-cube dyadic filtration. The result is cutoff-uniform and retains the rational coefficient exactly through its pointwise Pauli/Fierz bound. It proves a symbolic source-square constant in precisely defined L6 operator norms; it does not numerically enclose those norms or close the production sextic budget.

theorem.pauli_operator: For the production coefficients and every psi in C^3, 0<=B(psi)<=beta_op |psi|^2 I_6, beta_op=4(a+2b+c)=0.0423749999999894. The upper constant is sharp on a doublet tangent direction and includes the fixed floor and third component.
theorem.sharp_shell: For shell j outside the previous cube N_(j-1), kappa_j=(2pi/L)(N_(j-1)+1), and ||G_j^*F||_2^2<=M_R^2/[c_sym(1+kappa_j^2)] ||F||_2^2. The source contains one G_j and therefore M_R^2, not M_R^4.
theorem.vector_bounds: The strict dyadic sharp-cube maximal operator and the exact-weight derivative-prefix square function have finite cutoff-independent Hilbert-valued L6 norms M_6 and Q_6. A de la Vallee Poussin comparison plus periodic product Marcinkiewicz variation proves the bounds; a six-linear paraproduct multiplier gives an independent route after the pointwise B envelope.
theorem.source_square: sum_j ||G_j^* B(P_<=j-1 phi) D P_<=j-1 phi||_2^2 <= C_src ||phi||_6^6 with C_src=(beta_op^2/c_sym) M_R^2 M_6^4 Q_6^2.
theorem.production_base: beta_op^2/c_sym=0.016570372383568618. At p=1.1 and M_R=1, a source-only direct determinant budget would require M_6^4 Q_6^2<29.62571266025876. This is a target, not an established numerical enclosure.

harmonic_constants.M_6: The least constant in ||sup_j |P_<=j f|||_6<=M_6||f||_6 for R^6-valued f on T_L^3 and the strict dyadic sharp cubes.
harmonic_constants.Q_6: The least constant in ||(sum_j (1+kappa_j^2)^(-1)|D P_<=j-1 f|^2)^(1/2)||_6<=Q_6||f||_6, with all three derivatives and six real components.
harmonic_constants.proof_route: Choose a product de la Vallee Poussin cutoff equal to one on each sharp cube. The sharp-minus-smooth remainder has one-cube-annular support. Random signed remainders and normalized derivative shells obey uniform periodic product-Marcinkiewicz mixed-variation bounds. Khintchine and scale Young yield M_6,Q_6<infinity without a multiparameter Carleson assumption.
harmonic_constants.alternative_route: After |B(u)Du|^2<=beta_op^2|u|^4|Du|^2, polarization gives six-linear sharp-cube forms. Their scale multiplier has absolute value at most one and uniform dyadic face variation, so the multilinear product-Marcinkiewicz/paraproduct theorem gives the same cutoff-uniform conclusion.

honesty_boundary.warning: Finite FFT or multiplier samples do not prove the infinite-cutoff vector theorem and cannot supply a certified decimal M_6^4 Q_6^2. The obsolete A10 epsilon_6 allocation is not reused.

references: L. Grafakos and L. Slavikova, The Marcinkiewicz multiplier theorem revisited, arXiv:1706.07201.
